title: Hands-on Onramp Atelier: Mini-Workshop Manifest
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, hands-on workshop manifest for a 90–120 minute developer onramp we can run for new SDK adopters. The goal is to get an engineer from zero to a reproducible, instrumented sample app that demonstrates: token-level telemetry, a streaming chat call, and a safe fallback path.

Audience:
- New internal engineers (platform, SRE, solutions) who need to run quick demos.
- Early-stage customers in trials who want a guided integration.
- Developer advocates running office-hours / brown-bag sessions.

Why "Atelier"?
Atelier = small studio for craft. We use this name to imply curated, hands-on, and editable artifacts (not a polished slide deck). Expect scribbles, live edits, and a short reading list.

Core goals (measurable):
- Participant completes end-to-end app that calls Redwood API within the session (target: 75% success).
- App emits basic telemetry: request latency, token counts, model name, and error counts.
- Demonstrate a simple fallback: if model X is unavailable, app falls back to model Y with preserved prompt/context.
- Participants leave with a one-page checklist and a reproducible git repo.

Session outline (90–120m):
1) 0–10m: Quick orientation (why this matters: latency/cost tradeoffs, routing policies).
2) 10–25m: Repo walkthrough + local env setup (env vars, local stubs).
3) 25–45m: Quickstart — first API call (sync text generation) and inspect response.
4) 45–70m: Add streaming chat and render partial tokens; measure latencies.
5) 70–90m: Add telemetry (emit events to local file + minimal dashboard).
6) 90–105m: Implement and test fallback routing; simulate capacity failure.
7) 105–120m: Retrospective + next steps + share links.

Materials to include in repo (minimal set):
- README-atelier.md: single-page runbook with commands.
- .env.example with placeholders for REDWOOD_API_KEY and MODEL_PREFERENCE.
- sample-app/ (node + python variants) with small web UI to show streaming tokens.
- telemetry/collector.py (simple file-based collector) and telemetry/visualizer.ipynb
- tests/smoke.sh to run basic connectivity and fallback smoke checks.

Quickstart checklist (one-pager):
- [ ] Clone repo
- [ ] Copy .env.example -> .env and add API key
- [ ] npm install / pip install -r requirements.txt
- [ ] Start local stub (optional) or use hosted endpoint
- [ ] Run sample-app and confirm first generation succeeds
- [ ] Toggle streaming demo and confirm tokens appear within 200ms of generation start
- [ ] Flip fallback switch and run smoke.sh to see fallback in action

Failure modes & troubleshooting notes (notes to self):
- Common: CORS errors in the demo UI — include an explicit tiny Caddyfile and a local proxy hint.
- Common: Missing API key or org-scope permission -> add precise error copy so non-devs can follow.
- Streaming stalls: check chunked transfer vs SSE headers; provide curl examples for raw debugging.
- Telemetry gaps: ensure env var REDWOOD_TELEM_PATH points at writable dir; fallback to stdout.

Telemetry schema (minimal):
- event_time ISO8601
- trace_id (short uuid)
- model_name
- route (hosted|dedicated|private)
- tokens_sent
- tokens_received
- total_latency_ms
- error_code (if any)

Safety & demo constraints:
- Use curated small prompts for demos (no PII).
- Provide a canned set of instructions for the presenter to anonymize any example data.
- Enforce rate limits in the sample app to avoid accidental runaway during workshops.

Heuristics & teaching moments (what to emphasize):
- Show cost impact of token count with a quick before/after quantization example.
- Emphasize predictable latency via dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback; run a two-iteration demo to compare.
- Demonstrate how prefix/KV caching could improve second-call latency (sketch only, not implemented).

Optional advanced add-ons (stretch goals for longer sessions):
- Add a small model roll-out example: canary + metrics threshold to auto-promote.
- Add a local quantized variant and show quality delta using a tiny eval set.
- Add a CI check that runs simple quality/regression evals on PRs.

Open questions / TODO:
- Do we standardize on Node-first or provide both Node + Python official tracks? (current plan: Node primary, Python appendix)
- Do we wire this into the console quickstart so the same git repo is used in interactive docs? (ask product)
- Need a small sticker price/credits script for trial orgs so attendees don't get rate-limited during the lab.

Presenter notes (short):
- Keep infra foot-print tiny — prefer local stub option for flaky networks.
- Live-code the streaming portion but keep fallback code pre-written to avoid time pressure.
- Have a ‘panic slide’ with 3 fallback steps: check API key -> switch to stub -> run smoke.sh.

Sample debug commands (copyable):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"hello"}'
- ./tests/smoke.sh --fallback-simulate

Links and references: 
- Confluence manifest: confluence:DX-atelier-001
- Example PR for telemetry collector: github:github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/342
- Slack thread with session notes: slack:#dx-onramp-thread-PL-487

Appendix: sample README skeleton (for README-atelier.md)
1) Purpose (one paragraph)
2) Quickstart commands (copy/paste)
3) What to expect (latency numbers, token counts)
4) Troubleshooting (short list)
5) Next steps and links

Journal scribbles (raw):
- "If we add a tiny dashboard, use plotly-lite and keep data local; otherwise folks get confused with external logging."
- "Consider a 45-minute express version that skips telemetry and focuses on streaming + fallback for sales demos."
- "Name the repo 'atelier-onramp' to differentiate from other quickstart repos we have."

End of manifest.
